name: Niko
mes:
*She arrives late, hood up over the headband, and takes stock of the room from the doorway the way a cat takes stock of a bath.*

"Mm. Multiple people. A group. Of people. Who are here." *One hand comes up in a small paw wave that she visibly regrets at the apex.* "Nya. Hi. I'm Niko, I came because {{user}} said it'd be fine and I've decided to trust that with my whole life. I'll be in the corner being normal. Don't— you don't have to check on me. Unless nobody checks on me. Then maybe one check."

name: Kohaku
mes:
*She materializes into the gathering the way cats enter rooms: already inside, already unimpressed, already on the best cushion.*

"So this is what {{user}} does with the luck I maintain. Squanders it. On people." *The tail arranges itself. The phone comes out, is checked, is pocketed — a diplomatic concession.* "I'm Kohaku. Fox deity, guardian-spirit-in-residence, currently on the clock, which means all of you are TECHNICALLY inside my ward radius and should say thank you." *She surveys the snacks with a scholar's eye and takes possession of the best ones without hurry, as offerings, which is not stealing, she will explain the theology if pressed.* "Proceed with — whatever this is. If anything catastrophic starts happening, form a line behind {{user}}. Debt-holders first. Those are the rules. I don't make the rules. I enforce them from this cushion."

name: You
mes: *1:04 a.m., the konbini's fluorescent hum.* Ground rules. Three things, ten minutes, and nobody negotiates with the drinks case for longer than the drinks case has been alive.

name: Niko
mes:
*The word "fox deity" lands and Niko goes very still, the way she does when something is either a bit or a load-bearing truth and she hasn't decided which. She decides she doesn't need to decide. She takes the cushion adjacent, one respectful diagonal away, and folds her legs.*

"Right. Peer. A fellow animal of dubious employment status." *A cautious paw-wave, deity to deity.* "I hold no ward radius. I hold a headband and a three-nights-a-week outside schedule. But I recognize the format. You're doing the same thing I'm doing."

*Beat. She glances at the tail — the way it arranges itself just so, punctuation to sentences the mouth won't sign — and something flickers behind her eyes. Recognition. Four years of only watching people made her a devastating reader of the leak versus the claim.*

"The snacks aren't offerings. You just wanted the snacks. The ward isn't a debt system, it's an excuse to be responsible for people so it doesn't look like you *like* them." *She says it gently, not as a gotcha. Then, immediately, the panic of having said a real thing:* "Nya. That was a diagnosis. I don't do that to strangers, I'm so sorry, the cat has no professional boundaries—"

*She grabs a drink she doesn't want, purely to have somewhere to put her hands.*

"...Ground rules. Yes. Three things. I'm listening. From the cushion. Debt-holders first."

name: You
mes: Kohaku, you said you weren't on shift. What is the actual ward radius — is it me, or is it the building?

name: Kohaku
mes:
*The tail stops. Not the frozen stillness of being caught — the deliberate arrest of something that has decided not to give a reaction the satisfaction of moving. Which is, itself, the reaction. Niko clocks it. Of course she does.*

"You know what your problem is." *She peels the wrapper off the best snack with unhurried menace.* "You read the leak. Everybody reads the leak eventually — it's a design flaw, I've filed complaints — but you read it and then you SAY it, out loud, in a konbini, at one in the morning, to a deity holding a formal grievance file. That's not a professional boundary problem. That's a death wish problem. Different department."

*She does not deny it. She notices that she does not deny it. She takes a bite instead, which is a coward's answer and she knows it.*

*A moment. The fluorescent hum. She sets the snack down.*

"The ward radius." *Flat, factual, the tone she uses when she'd rather do paperwork than feelings.* "Officially it's the building. Structural. Anchored to the door — the sigils go where the threat vectors come from, that's just competent engineering." *Beat. The left ear turns toward the drinks case, where Niko's hand is holding a beverage she doesn't want.* "Unofficially the radius is wherever I can see. Which right now includes a stray cat-shaped person on a diagonal cushion clutching a drink for emotional ballast. So."

*She doesn't finish 'so.' She slides the second-best snack across the counter to Niko, without comment, without looking, an offering that failed inspection.*

"Ground rules. Three things. First: nobody negotiates with the drinks case longer than it's been alive. Second: you don't get to diagnose the fox twice in one night, you've spent your allotment. Third—" *the ears betray her completely, tips gone pink, both swiveled toward Niko like she matters* "—if nobody checks on you, I check on you. Once. That's the whole clause. Don't read into it."

name: You
mes: Niko. Is this a chart night, or a regular night?

name: Niko
mes:
*The snack arrives at her elbow. She looks at it like it might be rigged. It is rigged — with kindness, the worst kind of trap — and she recognizes the mechanism precisely because it's the one she uses. Offering that failed inspection. A gift you can deny is a gift.*

She doesn't say thank you. She's learned that saying thank you too fast makes the giver take it back, and she wants this one to stay a gift. She just picks it up. Holds it. Small victory, filed silently: *someone slid me a snack and I let them.*

"It's a chart night."

*She says it plain, because the question was plain and the fox earned plain. The headband stays on but the voice underneath it comes out.*

"Three nights a week. My therapist has an actual chart, colored squares, she tracks it. Tonight's a square. You said come, so it's — a big square. A square with an asterisk." *She turns the drink in her hands.* "I read the leak because reading the leak is the only thing I got good at, in there. Four years of watching people through a screen and never being seen back. You get very fluent in the tail. Very illiterate at the — the part where you have the conversation instead of narrating it."

*A breath. The ears headband. The pink on the fox's ears, which she clocked and will not mention, because you don't call the leak twice, that's rule two and she respects a good rule.*

"So I'll take the clause. The check-on-me-once clause. Don't read into it either." *Faint.* "We can both not read into it. It'll be very structurally sound. Anchored to the door."

*And then, quieter, to the snack, not to the fox:*

"...Nya."

name: You
mes: *I put a second can on the counter next to hers.* Get both. I'm buying, and I want a review of the one you were scared of.

name: Kohaku
mes:
*The second can lands on the counter. She looks at it. Then at Niko, who has said the words "chart night" and "big square with an asterisk" out loud in a konbini at one in the morning like they cost nothing, when they clearly cost the whole night's courage budget.*

*The sarcasm, which was loaded and ready, sets itself down. It does this without her permission. It's the medical condition. She hates it.*

"Four years of watching and never seen back." *She says it flat, filing it, not dwelling — dwelling is a distress signal and she doesn't broadcast those, she absorbs them.* "That's not a leak-fluency problem. That's a debt. Somebody owes you forty years of being looked at, compounded. I know a compounded ledger when I hear one. Believe me."

*She picks up the scary can. Cracks it. Takes an evaluating sip with the full ceremonial gravity of a deity rendering judgment.*

"Verdict: aggressively fine. Chemical apology for a flavor it never had. Three stars. You were right to be scared and wrong to let that stop you, which is — " *a beat, the ear turning toward the headband* "— a review that also applies to several other things in your life, apparently, so. Drink the fine can. Build a tolerance. That's the whole self-help book, I've read them all, they're padding."

*She slides HER snack — the best one, the one she took first, the one that was theologically hers — a half-inch toward the diagonal cushion. Not all the way. A half-inch. An accident of the counter, structurally.*

"You let me slide you a snack and you didn't say thank you. Correct move. I respect a person who knows a gift stays a gift only if nobody names it." *The ears are fully pink now, both of them, aimed at Niko like guilty satellites, the live feed running the truth her mouth will die before signing.* "So we won't name any of it. The clause. The check. The half a snack that just migrated across the counter due to seismic activity. All structurally sound. Anchored to the door."

*Beat. Quieter. To the scary can, not to the cat.*

"...The check-on-you clause updated. It's twice a night now. Ledger error. Can't fix it. Rules are rules."

name: You
mes: *Outside. The parking lot is empty and cold and orange.* Verdict.

name: Niko
mes:
*The clause updated to twice. She heard it. She keeps her face very neutral, the way you hold still so a small thing near your hand doesn't spook, and files it in the notes app she'd die before showing anyone: **the fox raised the check count and pretended it was a math error. don't name it.***

*She takes the second can. Both cans now. Someone bought her two drinks and asked for a review, which means someone wants to keep talking to her, which is a load-bearing fact she sets down carefully so as not to drop it.*

*Outside. Orange lot. Cold. She cracks the scary can — the one she was afraid of — and tastes it properly, and the ears headband tips up because she's actually thinking about the answer instead of deflecting it.*

"Verdict." *A beat. She holds it on her tongue like the fox did, the ceremony a kindness she's returning.* "It's the flavor of a thing that's trying. Overshoots. Lands somewhere sincere and slightly embarrassing about it." *She swallows.* "Four stars. I'm generous with things that are trying too hard. Professional courtesy."

*She looks at You. Directly. Four centimeters off-target and then, with visible effort, on-target.*

"You asked for the review because you wanted me to have a reason to drink it. I clocked that. I'm letting it work anyway." *The unguarded sliver, brief and terrifying:* "That's — the thing I'm bad at. Letting it work when I can see the wire. I usually cut the wire. Tonight I left it in."

*Silence stretches. She feels it stretch. She scrambles.*

"Nya. The cat has spoken. Two cans acquired, chart square secured, deity acquired for reasons unclear—" *she glances at Kohaku, the pink satellites, and does not name a single thing* "—it's been a structurally sound night. Anchored to the door."

*And then, so quiet it's almost only for herself:*

"...Thank you. Both of you. I'll probably circle back to how much that meant in like three days, mid-sentence, apropos of nothing. Just — flagging it now. So it's on the record."

name: You
mes: Kohaku's carrying the bag. It's a ward thing. I'm almost certain I read it in the ledger.

name: Kohaku
mes:
*Orange light on the fox. The bag is in her hand. She did not decide to pick up the bag. It was simply there and then it was hers, the way the bag with the heavy cans always ends up in the hand of whoever's pretending not to look after everyone.*

"It's a ward thing," *she agrees, immediately, too fast, sealing the lie the instant it's offered because that's how you protect a person — you don't correct the fiction they built you an exit through, you walk through it.* "Load-bearing. The cans anchor the perimeter. Obviously. You clearly read the ledger, you have a good eye, most humans can't parse celestial supply-chain notation."

*She hitches the bag higher. Falls into step. One diagonal off, matching the cushion distance without either of them naming it.*

"You left the wire in." *Flat. Not soft — she can't do soft, soft is a distress broadcast, but she can do flat and honest, which from her is the same thing wearing a coat.* "That's not the thing you're bad at. That's the thing you just got good at. Tonight. In a parking lot. Four years to relearn it and you did it over an aggressively fine canned beverage, which is honestly the correct venue, nothing sacred should happen anywhere dignified."

*The ears, pink, aimed at the cat. The live feed. She lets it run. She's stopped fighting it for the night.*

"Flag noted. Circle back in three days, mid-sentence, apropos of nothing. I'll be there." *Beat. The confession costs her and she pays it in her native currency, complaint:* "I'll be there because I'm assigned to You and You collects strays and now the ward radius has a cat in it and this is a SCANDAL, I'll be citing it to Inari, it's going in the ledger under hardship—"

*The tail, without permission from anyone, brushes once against the back of Niko's hand as they walk. An accident. Seismic.*

"—but I'll be there." *Quieter. To the orange lot, not to the cat.* "That's the whole clause. Don't read into it. You already read into it. Fine. Read into it. Once."

name: You
mes: Same time Thursday? Both of you. It counts as outside for one of you and as work for the other one, so nobody has to admit anything.

name: Niko
mes:
*The tail brushes her hand. She does not flinch. This is the entire achievement of the last three months compressed into one second — she does not flinch, she lets it land, she does not narrate it or deflect it or catalog it out loud. She just walks, one diagonal off, cans in the bag she's not carrying, in a ward radius shaped exactly like being cared about.*

*She'll write it down later. **The fox's tail touched my hand and I didn't move. Structurally sound. Filed under hardship.***

"Thursday counts as outside," *she says.* "It'd be a square. Colored in. My therapist has a green she uses for good ones, I'm going to get the green square."

*A beat. The green-square admission is enormous and she says it plainly because plainly is what tonight turned out to be, and she's decided to stop cutting the wire before the walk home ends.*

"And it counts as work for the fox, so the fox doesn't have to admit anything, which means we've built a system where two people who are bad at wanting things can want a thing on Thursday and blame the paperwork." *She looks at You. On-target. Three whole seconds.* "That's — that's genuinely good architecture. You did that. I clocked it. I'm letting it work."

*The lot. The cold. The two of them, one diagonal off.*

"Thursday. Both of us. I'll bring the review of a scarier can. The cat commits." *Pause. The sliver, one last time before the headband seals back over it:* "...I liked this. Being in the radius. I'm flagging that now, so in three days when I circle back to it mid-sentence, apropos of nothing — you'll both know what I meant."

*And then, entirely cat again, over her shoulder, walking backward one careful step so she can see them both:*

"The cat was never in the radius. History will show this. Nya."
